recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. The current source already satisfies the seed issue, and duplicating the guidance on the Subscription resource page would add maintenance drift without changing implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-13100 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked for a non-substantive Subscription note clarifying that in FHIR the server combines publisher and information distributor roles, that other publish/subscribe architectures may use separate agents, and that implementers may use separate agents or other pub/sub architectures, with a W3C pub/sub reference.
initial_application: The request was applied by git-svn commit fdb5a42e7f20cd96dbd928c5a09d20c36e75338c, subject 'GF#13100 - subscription reference', corresponding to SVN revision 14490. That commit added the requested paragraph to source/subscription/subscription-introduction.xml with FHIRcast and W3C WebSub references.
additional_context: The R5 Subscriptions framework rewrite in dbeb5e6a7aa3cba0705a1c337c0eaf6174d32eb2 moved the architecture guidance from the resource introduction into source/subscriptions.html. The current Subscription resource introduction now points to subscriptions.html for general Subscription guidance, and source/hierarchy.xml lists subscriptions.html in the built specification. Targeted Zulip and Confluence searches found no substantive community discussion conflicting with the Jira/source history; Zulip only showed tracker/commit bot notifications for GF#13100.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scoped source at source/subscriptions.html states that the FHIR server combines publisher and information distributor roles, notes that some publish/subscribe arrangements separate the roles, says the specification makes no recommendation about internal server architecture, and includes adjacent FHIRcast/W3C WebSub relationship text.

related_jiras.note: Its R5 implementation commit moved the Subscription architecture paragraph into source/subscriptions.html while addressing a separate max-count request; it was context only, not part of this decision.
